text: The 2025 Bear Gulch Fire (~20,000+ acres) burned into the Staircase/Lake Cushman and North Fork Skokomish area; several trails there (Mt. Rose, Mildred Lakes, Dry Creek, Copper Creek) remain closed through Oct 1, 2026, though FS-24 and the Staircase developed area reopened July 8, 2026. This is a different drainage from the South Fork Skokomish/Six Ridge approach used for Olson and doesn't directly affect it, but verify current trail and road status before a trip.
Closed to motor vehicles beyond the washout (closed since Jan. 2002); open to foot, bike, and horse traffic on the old roadbed
As of late October 2026 the Elwha road stays closed to vehicles at the Madison Falls parking area because of a washout, with walkers and cyclists allowed through and no reopening date set.

From US-101 near Lake Crescent, follow Sol Duc Hot Springs Road roughly 14 miles past the resort to the road-end parking area. The Elwha-side alternative via Whiskey Bend is a genuine second approach to this peak but has no car access: Olympic Hot Springs Road is closed to vehicles beyond Madison Falls by a washout, with no reopening date, adding a 6.2-mile one-way walk or bike to reach Whiskey Bend.

The Olympic Hot Springs Road (drive to Whiskey Bend Trailhead) is washed out and closed to vehicles beyond Madison Falls, with no reopening date; it is open to walkers and bikes. The Bailey Range Traverse beyond Cat Basin (which includes the approach to Barnes) was closed during the August 2023 Olympic lightning fires and can be re-closed in future high fire-danger periods; check current fire/trail conditions with the WIC. The Elwha River Trail exit can be affected by seasonal washouts or a Dodger Point closure that forces a longer alternate route.

Begins about 8 miles east of the Hurricane Ridge Visitor Center; narrow and winding with sheer drop-offs and few guardrails. Check the NPS Current Road Conditions page before driving. The alternative Dosewallips River Road approach is closed to vehicles (washout since 2002) and requires a long walk or bike-in to reach the actual trailhead.

Open — FS-24 and the Staircase developed area reopened July 8, 2026 after the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire closure, but the North Fork Skokomish River Trail beyond the Staircase Rapids Loop and the Flapjack Lakes Trail (this route's approach) remain closed, with no announced reopening date. Check with Olympic National Park before you go.

The standard approach is still closed: FS-24 and the Staircase developed area reopened July 8, 2026 after the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire (contained November 12, 2025), but the North Fork Skokomish River Trail beyond the Staircase Rapids Loop and the Flapjack Lakes Trail remain closed for hazard assessment and repairs, with no reopening date on the park's fire-conditions page updated September 18, 2026. Check with Olympic National Park before planning a trip.

The road is open (FS-24 reopened July 8, 2026), but the North Fork Skokomish trail out of Staircase remains closed beyond the Staircase Rapids Loop after the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire, with no end date given as of the Olympic National Park fire-conditions page updated September 18, 2026 — check current trail status before committing to this approach.

The Duckabush River Trail is open: the park's Bear Gulch Fire closures are on the Staircase side (the North Fork Skokomish, Home Sweet Home and Six Ridge trails), with no reopening date on the park's trail-conditions page updated September 14, 2026, and no Forest Service alert lists the Duckabush road or trail.

The North Fork Skokomish Trail out of Staircase has been closed since the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire, and so has the Home Sweet Home Trail from the Duckabush side up to First Divide, with no reopening date on the park's trail-conditions page (updated September 14, 2026) or fire-conditions page (updated September 18, 2026). The Duckabush Trailhead (off US-101 near Brinnon) and Duckabush Trail #803 toward Marmot Lake are open, but no open trail runs on from there to First Divide while the closure stands.

The road is open, but the approach is not: the North Fork Skokomish Trail from Staircase to First Divide and the Home Sweet Home Trail from First Divide down to the Duckabush River Trail junction have been closed since the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire (20,233 acres, contained 12 Nov 2025) while crews assess hazard trees and repair backcountry infrastructure, with no reopening date on the park's trail-conditions page (updated September 14, 2026) or fire-conditions page (updated September 18, 2026). Flapjack Lakes, Six Ridge, Wagonwheel Lake and First Divide camp are closed as well, so neither the Staircase side nor the Duckabush side has an open trail to First Divide while the closure stands.

Pavement ends ~1.7 mi onto FR-24 from Hoodsport, then ~3.7 mi of gravel to the Staircase Ranger Station/trailhead. The developed Staircase area reopened July 8, 2026 after a year-long closure from the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire, but surrounding wilderness trails - including the Flapjack Lakes/North Fork Skokomish Trail used for this route's approach - remain closed for post-fire repair, with no reopening date on the park's fire-conditions page updated September 18, 2026; verify before attempting.

Access is via the Staircase area of Olympic National Park (North Fork Skokomish). The Staircase developed area (road, campground, ranger station) was closed by the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire and reopened July 8, 2026, but the Flapjack Lakes and North Fork Skokomish trails beyond the developed area remain closed for hazard mitigation, with no reopening date on the park's fire-conditions page updated September 18, 2026 — confirm current road AND trail status before the trip.

The Flapjack Lakes/North Fork Skokomish Trail and surrounding backcountry have been closed since the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire (20,233 acres, 100% contained Nov 2025); the developed Staircase area itself reopened July 8, 2026, but the wilderness trails remain closed with no reopening date on the park's fire-conditions page updated September 18, 2026 - confirm current status with Olympic National Park before attempting this route.

As of the NPS trail-conditions update on 6/5/26, the Flapjack Lakes Trail and North Fork Skokomish River Trail are closed due to the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire, with no reopening date given — verify current status with Olympic National Park before this trip.

From US-101 at Lake Quinault take North Shore Road about 14 miles to the North/South Shore intersection, then North Fork Quinault Road about 4 miles to the trailhead and ranger station. North Shore is the only way in: South Shore Road is closed by a washout at about mile 8 from US-101, with no reopening date on Olympic National Park's alerts page updated August 27, 2026. The Elwha approach via Whiskey Bend is a genuine alternative but is foot and bike only: Olympic Hot Springs Road has been shut to vehicles beyond Madison Falls since November 2017 flood damage, adding roughly 7 miles each way.

Whiskey Bend Road has been closed to vehicles since November 2017 flood damage washed out Olympic Hot Springs Road beyond Madison Falls; Graves Creek Road (Quinault side) reopened May 2026 via a North Shore Road detour after a separate South Shore Road washout. Check the NPS Current Road Conditions page before any trip.
As of late October 2026 the Elwha road stays closed to vehicles at the Madison Falls parking area because of a washout, with walkers and cyclists allowed through and no reopening date set.

From US-101 at Lake Quinault take North Shore Road about 14 miles to the North/South Shore intersection, then North Fork Quinault Road about 4 miles to the trailhead and ranger station. North Shore is the only way in: South Shore Road is closed by a washout at about mile 8 from US-101, with no reopening date on Olympic National Park's alerts page updated August 27, 2026.

Elwha access road closed to vehicles beyond Madison Falls since November 2017 flood damage, with no reopening date on Olympic National Park's alerts page updated August 27, 2026; North Fork Quinault Road generally unaffected but may close seasonally in winter
As of late October 2026 the Elwha road stays closed to vehicles at the Madison Falls parking area because of a washout, with walkers and cyclists allowed through and no reopening date set.

As of the Olympic National Park road-conditions page updated August 7, 2026, Sol Duc Road is open to vehicles, but the Elwha-side Whiskey Bend Road remains closed to vehicle traffic (foot/bike only) due to flood damage, with no end date given -- verify current status before planning your exit.
As of late October 2026 the Elwha road stays closed to vehicles at the Madison Falls parking area because of a washout, with walkers and cyclists allowed through and no reopening date set.

Olympic Hot Springs Road beyond Madison Falls is closed to vehicles by a washout, with no reopening date, adding roughly 7 miles each way of walking or biking to reach the Whiskey Bend trailhead on the Elwha approach. On the Quinault side, South Shore Road has a separate washout closure near milepost 8 (use North Shore Road as the detour); Call the park's Road and Weather Hotline (360-565-3131) or check the park's road conditions page for current status before committing to either approach.
As of late October 2026 the Elwha road stays closed to vehicles at the Madison Falls parking area because of a washout, with walkers and cyclists allowed through and no reopening date set.

Olympic Hot Springs Road has been closed to vehicles beyond Madison Falls since November 2017 flood damage, with no reopening date on Olympic National Park's alerts page updated August 27, 2026, so reaching the Whiskey Bend trailhead adds roughly 7 miles of road approach each way — check NPS alerts before you go.

Campfires are prohibited above 3,500 ft; within the Flapjack Lakes/Gladys Divide quota zone, deviating from your permitted itinerary is not allowed except in emergencies. The Bear Gulch Fire closure still applies to this approach: FS-24 and the Staircase developed area reopened July 8, 2026, but the North Fork Skokomish River Trail beyond the Staircase Rapids Loop and the Flapjack Lakes Trail have been closed since the July 2025 fire, with no announced reopening date. Check with Olympic National Park before you go.

FS-24 and the Staircase developed area (campground, ranger station, trailhead) reopened July 8, 2026, after being closed since the July 2025 Bear Gulch Fire. However, the North Fork Skokomish Trail beyond the Staircase Rapids Loop — including the Flapjack Lakes Trail and campsite, the only approach to The Horn — remains closed while NPS crews complete hazard assessments and repair fire-damaged infrastructure, with no end date given as of the Olympic National Park fire-conditions page updated September 18, 2026. Check current NPS alerts before planning a climb.

The Staircase developed area and FS-24 access road reopened on July 8, 2026, following the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire closure. However, the North Fork Skokomish Trail beyond the Rapids Loop and the Flapjack Lakes Trail/campsite — the only practical approach to The Horn — remain closed while NPS crews complete hazard assessments and repair fire-damaged infrastructure (bridges, privies), with no end date given as of the Olympic National Park fire-conditions page updated September 18, 2026. Confirm current trail status with Olympic National Park before planning any trip.
